optional_codes.reason: Personal history of antineoplastic chemotherapy: describes the completed treatment, and no instruction requires it. Defensible either way.

unsupported_codes.reason: Malignant neoplasm of colon: reporting a code from this category treats the cancer as current, and the note documents that it was removed, that treatment ended and that there is no evidence of disease.

citations.Z08: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.C.2.m: when a primary malignancy has been previously excised or eradicated from its site, there is no further treatment directed to that site, and there is no evidence of any existing primary malignancy at that site, a code from category Z85 is used. Section I.C.21.c.8: follow-up codes explain continuing surveillance following completed treatment, and the follow-up code is sequenced first, followed by the history code. Here the colon cancer was removed in 2023, chemotherapy was completed in early 2024, there has been no treatment since, and colonoscopy, CT and tumor marker show no disease, so the visit is reported as a follow-up examination and the cancer is not reported as current, although the assessment opens with the words 'colon cancer'.
citations.Z85.038: Tabular List instruction at Z08: use additional code to identify the personal history of malignant neoplasm (Z85.-); instruction at Z85: code first any follow-up examination after treatment of malignant neoplasm (Z08). The inclusion term at Z85.038 is 'Conditions classifiable to C18'. Here the former site is the ascending colon.
citations.Z90.49: Tabular List instruction at Z08: use additional code to identify any acquired absence of organs (Z90.-). ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.B.7: a 'use additional code' note indicates that a secondary code should be added, if known. Here part of the colon was removed by right hemicolectomy.

coder_notes: Z08 is first-listed. No rule fixes the order of Z85.038 and Z90.49 after it. Z09 is not used: it is for conditions other than malignant neoplasm. The surveillance colonoscopy was an earlier encounter, so no screening or procedure-related code belongs to this visit.
